basics.name: Mike Beaumier
basics.headline: PhD physicist turned AI engineer and data scientist who leads products from prototype to launch

roles.title: Founder & Engineer
highlights: Reverse-engineered the binary format of TablEdit, a long-standing desktop tab editor, so 786 tabs that needed the desktop program now play, print, and edit in any browser, and published an open, diffable notation format that programs can read and edit

Built a library of 19,500+ bluegrass works by normalizing 15 sources in six formats into one record per song, with extraction ranging from custom HTML parsers to AI vision transcription of a handwritten 1981 songbook, and a searchable core of nearly 3,000 jam songs

Designed and built the whole stack, from a static site with a search index rebuilt in CI to a Postgres backend with row-level security, sign-in, and 11 serverless functions, so a musician's correction shows in seconds and is committed to the song's files, which redeploy once tests pass
Built a tab player that plays several instruments together in the browser, slowed down, looped, or in another key, and an editor where musicians write new tabs that play back

Partnered with YouTube banjo teacher Jim Pankey (156,000 subscribers, 20 million views) through cold outreach, landing a lesson video that sends viewers to the site's free tab; November 2026 brought 3,100+ new visitors, nearly five times October's
Ran bluegrassbook.com as a free, installable web app that keeps opened songs available offline, for under $5 a month
roles.summary: Song and tablature library for bluegrass musicians with about 7,000 visitors; founded it in May 2025, went full-time in November 2026, and owned product, engineering, and operations

roles.title: Founding Staff Data Scientist

projects.name: Established internal AI engineering platform for all developer workflows
highlights: Designed, built, evaluated, and launched the company's AI coding agent platform, doubling engineering coding output, measured with change-point analysis
Designed and built the agent workflow that takes a ticket to a merged pull request, delegating each stage to shared skills
Designed and built a single source format for the company's agent skills, transpiled per editor, so each skill installed correctly in Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode without forking the library
Authored the RFC for measuring whether coding agents follow the company's written instructions, separating whether an agent consulted an instruction from whether its output conformed
Led the rewrite of the company's AI developer platform in Rust, from proposal to the tool every engineer ran, shipping it in stages so no one lost tooling during the switch

projects.name: Designed and implemented company-wide AI code review tooling
highlights: Designed, built, evaluated, and launched an AI code reviewer in GitHub that took first-round review off engineers and cut time to approval 41-56% on size-matched changes by ending drawn-out multi-round review threads
Cut the AI code reviewer's cost to about a tenth of an engineer's review by redesigning it around one higher-quality agent

Designed and built a benchmark of human-reviewed pull requests, stratified by coding style, size, and domain: running without developer oversight, 89.1% of the AI reviewer's findings matched a human reviewer's
Ran the head-to-head evaluation of AI code-review approaches that set the company's choice, picking a reviewer that caught nearly all known issues at a fraction of the cost

projects.name: Transformed and hardened vulnerability detection workflows
highlights: Automated the building of an interpretable classifier that matched the company's foundation-model vulnerability detector: a self-improving agent loop read its errors, wrote features from a security-knowledge library, and kept what helped

Designed and built an expert-in-the-loop annotation platform pairing structured LLM analysis (Pydantic AI) with expert review, which produced the company's gold-standard evaluation set for vulnerability detection in compiled code
Showed LoRA matching full fine-tuning of a 110M-parameter transformer for vulnerability detection in compiled code while training 1.07% of its parameters
Shaped the research direction toward agentic approaches with evidence from expert review, gradient-boosted baselines, and a LoRA study

projects.name: Multi-agent orchestration and agent memory
highlights: Designed and built a multi-agent orchestrator that ran parallel coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) to plan, write, review, and validate code autonomously over multi-hour runs, before such tools were standard

Separated real defects from style preferences in code from parallel coding agents by having a second vendor's model (Claude or OpenAI) review each agent's work and arbitrating disagreements before merge

Built long-term memory for coding agents, a Claude Code plugin with session hooks and durable journals, so what an agent learned carried across sessions and context compaction instead of being rediscovered

Built a service that condensed each coding-agent session (Claude Code, OpenCode) into a searchable, secret-redacted briefing with capped spend, so a person or another agent could resume after a crash or handoff

projects.name: Vulnerability engine in the production product
highlights: Built the full backend stack for running the company's vulnerability-detection engine in its production product: session management, APIs, and persistence, with resource allocation and fault tolerance
Made the company's vulnerability engine build outside its author's environment for the first time, tracing its failures to a lockfile mismatch and a silent merge conflict that git never flagged
Ran the engine's first end-to-end scan on paid model calls, in which the engine correctly identified every function it escalated as a use-after-free memory bug
Audited the engine against product requirements and documented the gaps to close before customers could use it

projects.name: Backend for the company's software-vetting product
highlights: As backend lead, built and shipped the Rust API for a dashboard sales was waiting on, showing a customer which third-party software its security policy allows
Added live progress to long-running analyses end to end, from the analysis prompt through the report and list APIs, so users could follow an analysis instead of waiting on an opaque result
Adversarially tested the company's software-vetting product with a synthesized malicious binary posing as safe software, exposing a verdict flaw, and drove the fix to release

projects.name: Enterprise evaluation with a major app store
highlights: Opened an enterprise evaluation with a major app store's Android malware team through a former colleague, ran a live demo comparing the product's analysis with the buyer's internal tooling, and drove it to product-council review

Repositioned the product, which the buyer's engineers had filed as a static-analysis tool, as an AI agent that reverse engineers an app the way a skilled analyst does, mapped onto the app-store policies they already enforce

Delivered the product's fully automated analysis of a real Android threat when the buyer asked for evidence: an app that disguised itself after install and planted a backdoor that survived uninstalling
Opened a second channel into the same company's trust and safety organization, and coordinated the deal team across engineering leadership and go-to-market

projects.name: Redesigned and led engineering efforts to standardize all ML training operations as directed acyclic graphs
highlights: Designed and built the research team's Dagster pipeline platform through production Kubernetes, cutting environment setup from days to minutes and letting researchers launch GPU training jobs themselves

Kept the research team's self-service pipeline platform architecturally coherent as adoption grew, writing its guide and design doc and guiding teammates through review as they built 3 research pipelines on it

projects.name: Architected data provenance metadata registry for all data artifacts
highlights: Tech-led a provenance system for every dataset and model the company built: wrote the prototype and all design documents, set the direction, and guided junior engineers who built it into the shared data platform

projects.name: Research environment shared by people and coding agents
highlights: Designed and built a Jupyter research environment where humans and coding agents collaborated in shared live kernels through a custom MCP server, used by multiple researchers for 34 analyses over 4 months

Designed a persistent knowledge base for research agents, with auto-generated context and staleness tracking, so each new session started out knowing the team's research areas, datasets, and patterns across analyses
Fixed the real-time collaboration disconnects in an open-source Jupyter MCP server at the source, with the fixes merged upstream instead of carried as a local patch

projects.name: Hardened the build and merge path
highlights: Stopped pull requests that passed on their own from breaking the main branch together by adding merge-queue CI that tests the exact commit that will land
Made the team's git worktree tool safe for parallel use, closing race conditions and lock contention, and fixed a cleanup defect that could remove a developer's repository

Removed recurring build failures blocking the team, moving the binary-analysis toolchain from multi-gigabyte binary files to standard Python packages and fixing container builds that failed on network lookups

projects.name: Engineering standards and code review
highlights: Set the engineering team's code review standard as its most active reviewer, across domains from security to ML research, the standard its AI reviewer was later calibrated against
Standardized how engineers worked in the monorepo, with one entrypoint pattern (bootstrap, test, build, server) so any project could run without reading its README

Replaced hand-kept team directories that had drifted, leaving an engineer assigned as code owner with no notifications, with one machine-readable source that agents and CI read and that is checked for drift
Built LLM agents that condensed engineering activity, blockers, and tool releases across the company's systems into a daily Slack digest, which the head of business extended into a business report

roles.summary: AI security startup that finds vulnerabilities in compiled software; brought data science to its agentic development and its detection models, and built its AI developer platform, its code review automation, and backends for its customer product

roles.title: Senior Data Scientist, Ads Safety

projects.name: Gemini review agent for ad-policy reviewers
projects.summary: Reviewers worked with a keyword highlighter that marked policy terms with no sense of context. This agent, a Chrome extension built on an agent architecture, read each page and pointed reviewers to the parts most likely to violate ad policy.
highlights: Conceived, prototyped, architected, and led the launch of a Gemini-powered LLM agent that flagged ad-policy violations for Google's content reviewers, used in 40,000+ reviews a day and raising throughput 30% in A/B tests
Created the product area from nothing: defined its vision and roadmap, formed the working group, and won resources across teams and organizations to build it

Built and led the cross-functional team of engineers, analysts, and product managers that took the agent from prototype to production, and designed and built the A/B testing framework whose randomized controlled trials gated every launch
Architected the agent end to end, from the data infrastructure joining content crawling, ad serving, and review allocation to the LLM reasoning core and the Chrome extension

projects.name: Quality measurement for LLM content classifiers
highlights: Guided the design and validated the launch of Google's LLM auto-labeling classifiers, trusted only where the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval on precision cleared 80%, scaling review 10x across billions of web pages
Set Google Ads Safety's org-wide launch QA for LLM content classifiers, designing and building the sampling-and-review check for classifiers set to launch unchecked after tuning on dozens of examples

Built precision dashboards for Google's production LLM content classifiers on a continuous stream of human-reviewed samples, with bootstrapped confidence intervals to tell real drops from noise and flag underperformers

projects.name: Review efficiency for publisher safety
highlights: Let Google's publisher-safety reviewers cover 30% more content at higher precision by leading a working group that cut reviews of pages that never served ads and set a cost-per-impact metric
Raised enforcement up to 200x on some policies with high-precision rules running at over 80% precision

projects.name: Automatic Classification of Suspicious Web Content
highlights: Designed and built AutoML classifiers on SQL pipelines joining web-content signals with past human review outcomes, cutting manual review up to 80% across hundreds of millions of pages, saving millions a year
Searched thousands of model configurations with Google's AutoML, from linear models to deep networks, and deployed the best on SQL serving stacks after validating them against human review

projects.name: Ad Query Forecasting to Prioritize Content Review for New URLs
highlights: Found in ad-request logs the 90-minute window in which most of a new high-traffic page's harmful ad views can still be prevented, used it to shape the streaming system that flags such pages, and helped launch it, cutting those views 60% in the first 24 hours

Built the time-series data and modeling pipeline behind the forecasts, joining unstructured ad-request data with policy data, then folded it into the streaming system, retiring a separate pipeline for one simpler design

projects.name: Machine learning fairness for content classification
highlights: Led Google Ads Safety's ML fairness working group and set the org-wide bias metric for its content classifiers: false positive rate disparity on propensity-score-matched content, with human validation and hypothesis tests
Designed and scaled ML fairness measurement across Google's policy classifiers, finding classification disparities affecting protected groups and enabling their fixes

projects.name: Root causes of unwanted ad placements
highlights: Automated the monthly root-cause report on ads that appeared beside unsuitable content, with Python and SQL reports that pointed to where the system failed
Reviewed failure cases by hand to find the patterns behind them, giving monthly input for improving the content models and honoring advertisers' placement preferences

roles.summary: Google stops serving ads on web pages that break its content policies; built the forecasting, classifiers, and measurement that decided which of billions of pages human reviewers saw and which could be judged automatically

roles.title: Senior Data Scientist, Google Customer Solutions

projects.name: Revenue-based routing for new advertisers
highlights: Built the data and real-time pipelines for a team model that classified each new advertiser's 91-day revenue bucket to pick its sales treatment, routing $8B+ in revenue across 7M+ new advertisers
Gave a tabular AutoML revenue-routing model time-series awareness with trend-line features fit to each account's recent history, its largest gain: precision up 20%+ on high-spend advertisers

Mentored and onboarded new members of the team behind Google's $8B+ new-advertiser revenue-routing model, kept its data pipelines stable, wrote the model's documentation, and presented its results to leadership

projects.name: Incremental spend from a partner incentive fund
highlights: Scoped, built, and delivered a self-updating dashboard measuring the daily incremental spend of Google's channel sales partners from a multi-million-dollar incentive fund, using counterfactual time-series forecasts fit on pre-fund spend
Wrote the business requirements and design doc with the partner-incentives team, and built the pipeline tracking each partner's acquisitions

projects.name: Measuring sales-program incrementality
highlights: Wrote the requirements, built the data pipelines, and tech-led the team that shipped synthetic-control causal inference for 3 sales programs worth hundreds of millions of dollars where trials were not viable, validated on synthetic data and pre-treatment placebo tests
Moved the team onto sprints and retrospectives, improving its communication and on-time delivery, and refactored its incrementality pipelines into reusable, stable workflows

projects.name: Advertiser churn prediction
highlights: Built advertiser churn prediction end to end, from dataset and metrics to AutoML logistic-regression models and an automated lead pipeline and dashboard Google sales used to pick at-risk advertisers for high-touch outreach

Sized a churn-prevention pilot for Google's at-risk advertisers with iterative power analyses, including sensitivity to the churn rate, and designed the framework assigning advertisers to test and control groups

roles.summary: Google's sales teams can give personal attention to only a fraction of its advertisers; built the pipelines and models that helped choose which ones, and the measurement of whether that attention paid off

roles.title: Data Science Volunteer
highlights: Built analysis framework to measure text messaging campaign impact for Florida state-level elections.
Engineered engagement metrics and provided recommendations for voter turn-out campaigns.

roles.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
highlights: Led the final modeling stages of MBUX, Mercedes' 2018 flagship head-unit software, whose probabilistic graphical models predicted each driver's destinations, media, and calls from privacy-preserving in-car data
Built a reporting framework and predictive models of when vehicles would need service from Mercedes' global aftermarket data, informing marketing and helping dealerships prevent customer churn

Built the end-to-end data and ML pipeline for a mobile EV-charging pilot, from a daily vehicle-telemetry pipeline and stakeholder dashboard to models predicting battery state, destination, and parking time
Built Mercedes' first ML model of tire replacement, using hierarchical modeling to time proactive dealership outreach
Built and improved the consistency-testing framework for MBUX, Mercedes' 2018 flagship head-unit software, across multiple platforms
Built a Python decorator library that generated REST APIs and web UIs from plain Python functions
roles.summary: Machine learning for in-car personalization and vehicle service analytics

roles.title: Doctoral Researcher, Physics
highlights: Measured how W-boson production changes when the proton beam's spin is flipped, which shows how the proton's antiquarks are polarized, flavor by flavor; the analysis was foundational to Phys. Rev. D 98, 032007

Separated about 600 W decays from 15.7 billion collisions, where four in five surviving candidates were still background, with an extended unbinned maximum-likelihood fit using data to model background too rare to simulate

Result: the first such measurement with forward muons, indicating anti-up quarks spin with the proton more than earlier fits estimated; RHIC's W measurements together showed anti-up and anti-down quarks polarized oppositely, nearly cancelling
Helped build and test the resistive plate chambers (RPCs) that triggered on forward muons for PHENIX's W-boson measurement

Helped collect the 2013 polarized-proton dataset that makes up most of the published measurement's data, taking data-acquisition shifts, and managed petabyte-scale online data reconstruction for the experiment
Maintained and developed PHENIX's online spin monitor, the real-time check during data taking that the colliding proton beams are polarized in the intended direction and pattern
Ran parallel beam-collision simulations on high-performance computing clusters
Award-winning teaching assistant: top 2% of evaluations, with department and university teaching awards
roles.summary: PhD research in the PHENIX collaboration at Brookhaven's Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider, constraining the sea-quark contribution to the proton's spin through W-boson production.

roles.title: Data Science Fellow
highlights: Built "AleTrail," a full-stack web app for beer recommendations and customized pub crawls.
Scraped and processed brewery/review data; trained Naive Bayes classifier for beer flavor profiles.
Utilized Google Maps/Yelp APIs for geo-location and pub crawl generation.

roles.title: Undergraduate Researcher, Physics
highlights: Developed lab protocols to synthesize/characterize superparamagnetic nanoscale magnetite.

education.note: Thesis: Probing the Spin Structure of the Proton Using Polarized Proton-Proton Collisions and the Production of W Bosons

publications.title: Cross section and longitudinal single-spin asymmetry A_L for forward W±→μ±ν production in polarized p+p collisions at √s = 510 GeV
publications.contribution: Thesis analysis was foundational to this measurement, developed in a tight working group with Ralf Seidl, Francesca Giordano, Daniel Jumper, and Abraham Meles. Also helped build the resistive plate chambers (RPCs) that triggered on its forward muons, and helped collect the 2013 510 GeV dataset that makes up most of its data.

publications.title: Probing the Spin Structure of the Proton Using Polarized Proton-Proton Collisions and the Production of W Bosons
publications.venue: PhD thesis, University of California, Riverside
publications.contribution: Doctoral thesis constraining the sea-quark contribution to the proton's spin with W-boson production in PHENIX.

publications.title: Measurement of parity-violating spin asymmetries in W± production at midrapidity in longitudinally polarized p+p collisions
publications.contribution: Helped collect the 2013 510 GeV dataset, one of the three polarized p+p runs this measurement combines.
